incident_text: Users say their balances are out of date: trades made more than ten minutes ago do not show up.

E-001.claim: Config change at 12:00 raised holdings cache TTL from 60s to 1800s on portfolio-svc
E-001.author: reasoning

E-002.claim: After the change, portfolio-svc served holdings from cache with entry age growing to the new TTL
E-002.excerpt: 2026-03-30T12:09:18Z INFO portfolio-svc: serving holdings from cache, entry age 1800s
E-002.author: reasoning

E-003.claim: Cache staleness metric reached 1800s, matching the new TTL
E-003.author: reasoning

E-004.claim: portfolio-updates queue is healthy: no backlog, no DLQ
E-004.author: reasoning

E-005.claim: portfolio-consumer error rate is low and its throughput matches the publish rate
E-005.author: reasoning

E-006.claim: Redis showed no evictions, so the INC-0412 mechanism does not apply
E-006.author: reasoning

E-007.claim: The only other changes in the window were unrelated deploys before 11:30
E-007.author: reasoning

H1.statement: The HOLDINGS_CACHE_TTL_S increase from 60 to 1800 on portfolio-svc made holdings cache entries live up to 30 minutes. Reads therefore return stale balances even though the update pipeline is delivering data on time.

H2.statement: The portfolio-updates pipeline (aa-sync to portfolio-consumer) is lagging or dropping updates and so causing stale data.

H3.statement: A Redis eviction or restart caused a cache stampede, as in INC-0412.

notes: The cache log query was truncated (68 matches, 30 returned), so I did not see every log line after 12:11.
I did not confirm that portfolio-consumer writes invalidate or refresh the holdings cache. If they do not, even the old 60s TTL would show some staleness.
I did not check the exact time the first user reports began relative to 12:00. The staleness window only exceeds ten minutes from about 12:10 onward.
